title: Paul Cook - Wikipedia
notes: Paul Thomas Cook, born 20 July 1956, raised in Hammersmith; Christopher Wren School with Steve Jones. With Jones and Wally Nightingale formed the Strand (1972-73), which became the Sex Pistols. 'Cook's early influences included Motown, ska and glam rock acts like David Bowie, T. Rex, Roxy Music and Slade, in addition to drummers Kenney Jones of the Faces, Paul Thompson of Roxy Music, Al Jackson Jr. and Mitch Mitchell.' After the split (January 1978): the Great Rock 'n' Roll Swindle soundtrack with Jones, the Professionals (1979-82), Johnny Thunders' So Alone, Joan Jett, producing Bananarama's first album, Chiefs of Relief, Edwyn Collins's band from A Girl Like You, Man-Raze with Phil Collen, Vic Godard and Subway Sect; the Pistols' reunions from 1996 to 2008.

title: Sex Pistols - Wikipedia
notes: Formed in London in 1975; John Lydon, Steve Jones, Paul Cook, Glen Matlock (replaced by Sid Vicious in February 1977). Signed to EMI (October 1976), dropped January 1977; A&M (March 1977), dropped; Virgin (May 1977). Broke up after the San Francisco show of 14 January 1978.

title: Never Mind the Bollocks, Here's the Sex Pistols - Wikipedia
notes: Released 28 October 1977 (Virgin). 'Drummer Paul Cook, Jones and singer Johnny Rotten appear on every track'; Steve Jones played most of the bass after Matlock left; Vicious's bass on Bodies only. Produced by Chris Thomas and Bill Price at Wessex Sound Studios from March 1977; Heylin places God Save the Queen, Pretty Vacant, E.M.I. (and perhaps Did You No Wrong) in the March sessions, and No Feelings, Problems, Liar, New York, Seventeen and Submission among those Price produced while Thomas was away; Holidays in the Sun from 18 June; Bodies in August. Jones: he and Cook 'weren't just having a laugh' and were 'really dedicated in the studio'. Personnel: Paul Cook - drums.

title: Anarchy in the U.K. - Wikipedia
notes: The debut single, EMI, 26 November 1976; the EMI version recorded 17 October 1976, produced by Chris Thomas; number 38. Paul Cook - drums; Glen Matlock - bass.

title: God Save the Queen (Sex Pistols song) - Wikipedia
notes: Released 27 May 1977 (Virgin), number 2, banned by the BBC. Cook: 'it wasn't written specifically for the Queen's Jubilee. We weren't aware of it at the time.'

title: Pretty Vacant - Wikipedia
notes: Released 1 July 1977, the third single. The riff from ABBA's SOS (Matlock). The video filmed at ITN, Wells Street, London, on 11 and 12 July 1977. Cash Box: 'a straight forward rocker with upfront drumming'.

title: Holidays in the Sun (song) - Wikipedia
notes: Released 14 October 1977, the fourth single, number 8; written after the band's trips to Jersey and Berlin.

title: An Interview with Drummer Paul Cook of Sex Pistols and Manraze (Gail Worley, Ink 19, 29 November 2011)
notes: Experience before the Pistols: 'Hardly any, really... We were quite late starters'; 'It was all a learning process as we were going along'. 'We kept it simple, as we had to, because we were just learning our instruments'; 'not technically great at the time, so it was very tribal... That's where the power comes from.' Influences: Kenney Jones, Paul Thompson, Al Jackson ('a favourite'), 'loved Mitch Mitchell'; ska, Motown, T. Rex, Roxy Music, Slade, Hendrix. 'Me and Steve Jones grew up together, so we were really connected.' Playing with Edwyn Collins and Man-Raze 'improves you as a drummer, playing different styles'.

title: The drumming wisdom of Paul Cook (MusicRadar, 2015; read through the Bajaao copy)
notes: The writer: 'Take the perfectly-judged hats on God Save The Queen, the crash-laden Anarchy in the UK, or the tribal toms of Pretty Vacant': 'Cook's thoughtful kit work'. Cook: 'I listened to all of those drummers, Paul Thompson, Simon Kirke from Free'; 'Al Jackson I really liked'; 'Motown drummers as well I thought were really cool, with all those little rolls'. Chris Spedding (the 1976 demos) told them 'to just keep it simple and play 4/4 because that was the power of the band'. 'I was just accenting everything that Steve was playing'; 'When we recorded Never Mind The Bollocks we did it with just guitar and drums... We were a two-piece band.'
